text:
noah: Quick follow-ups from the runtime all-hands. Two themes: telemetry for kernel regressions and prioritization tradeoffs (latency vs cost).

ruth: I'll take telemetry. What exact signals do we want to expose to customers vs internal only?

noah: Internal: kernel-level opcode timings, quantize-fallback counts, microbatch size distribution. Customer-facing: p50/p95/p99 per model route + recent change tags.

jin: For kernel regressions we keep seeing a 7% throughput drop on afx GPUs after last patch. Are we sure it's kernel-level and not scheduling/batcher interaction?

ruth: Need to correlate kernel timestamps with batcher waits. Suggest adding a trace id to requests so we can stitch batcher start -> kernel launch -> finish.

sam: Tracing sounds heavy. Can we start with sampled traces (1%) and aggregated histograms for microbatch size and kernel exec time?

ruth: Yes, start sampled traces + 1s-resolution histograms aggregated per pool. We'll also report quantization fallback counts per hour.

anya: On prioritization: leadership wants to know impact of default conservative quantization vs aggressive quantization on cost and numeric parity. Can eng-research provide delta numbers?

jin: Research can run an eval across 20 representative routes this sprint and publish avg token cost delta + QA parity diff. Timeline: results by next Wed.

noah: For customers who care about shortest tails, can we auto-disable microbatching for requests with "latency_hint: low"?

sam: That is doable at the sidecar routing layer. We'll add a route hint check and bypass batching for latency_hint=low. Low latency will pay cost premium.

ruth: Action items: 1) Telemetry PR to include: sampled traces, histograms for batch size & kernel exec, quant-fallback counter (owner: ruth, due Fri). 2) Eval run for quantization tradeoffs (owner: jin, due Wed). 3) Sidecar flag for latency_hint bypass (owner: sam, due next Tue).

ops-bot: deploy-check: telemetry-collector -> canary passed (3/3).

noah: Thanks. Please post short README with dashboards and how to interpret the quant-fallback counter. We'll relay to PMs and support.

anya: Also ping support with a blurb for customers about opt-in aggressive quantization vs conservative defaults.

ruth: Will draft dashboards + README.

noah: Great, closing this thread—we'll reconvene in next eng sync on status. :wave:
